The following **list of best-selling music artists** includes those music acts from the 20th century to the present with claims of 75 million or more [record sales](Record_sales "Record sales") worldwide. This information cannot be listed officially, as there is no organization that has recorded global music sales.

The tables are listed with each artist's claimed sales figure(s) and their total independently certified units and are ranked in descending order by claimed sales. If two or more artists have the same claimed sales, they are then ranked by certified units. The claimed sales figure and the total of certified units (for each country) within the provided sources include sales of albums, singles, compilation-albums, music videos as well as downloads of singles and full-length albums. Sales figures, such as those from <SoundScan>, which are sometimes published by *[Billboard](Billboard_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")* magazine, have not been included in the certified units column.

## Definitions

Gold/Platinum certifications issued after 2016, especially on singles, are in some cases more than 50% streaming generated. Some of the 20th century artists can also have significant amount of streaming based certifications. The certified units of the newer artists may sometimes be higher than their listed claimed figures. This is because [Recording Industry Association of America](Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA) and almost all other certifying bodies count streaming towards Gold and Platinum thresholds required for Digital Single Award certification.[[1]](List_of_best-selling_music_artists#cite_note-1)[[2]](List_of_best-selling_music_artists#cite_note-2)[[3]](List_of_best-selling_music_artists#cite_note-3) For this reason, some singles and even albums get over certified by hundreds of thousands of units. The over certified figures, however, are often in millions of units for RIAA certifications, one such example is Rihanna's single "[We Found Love](We_Found_Love "We Found Love")", which is certified at nine times Platinum by the RIAA, yet during the time of the certification, it had sold 5.4 million downloads.[[4]](List_of_best-selling_music_artists#cite_note-4)[[5]](List_of_best-selling_music_artists#cite_note-5)

The certified units for some artists/bands who have multi-disc albums can be higher than their listed claimed figures due to the RIAA counting each unit within set as one unit toward certification. The certified units also can be inflated by the redundancy of certifications, because each of tracks downloads and streams contributed to the certifications of both of the single and the respective album. The RIAA counts 10 downloads of individual track as well as 1,500 audio/video streams as [an equivalent](Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit") to one unit of album, including those from singles released prior to the album release.[[6]](List_of_best-selling_music_artists#cite_note-6) Theoretically, if one song were streamed 1.5 billion times on <YouTube>, the single would receive [Diamond](List_of_best-selling_singles_in_the_United_States "List of best-selling singles in the United States") and the whole album could be certified Platinum,[[7]](List_of_best-selling_music_artists#cite_note-7) thus creating a combined total of 11 million certified units without any sales. [Kanye West](Kanye_West "Kanye West")'s album *[The Life of Pablo](The_Life_of_Pablo "The Life of Pablo")* achieved Platinum without selling a single copy and was only available for streaming.[[8]](List_of_best-selling_music_artists#cite_note-8)

Issued certifications for songs which have been recorded by multiple artists including featured artists are added to each artist's total amount of certified units, as all the artists would have played a significant part in a song. For example, "[This Is What You Came For](This_Is_What_You_Came_For "This Is What You Came For")" and "[Where Them Girls At](Where_Them_Girls_At "Where Them Girls At")" include Rihanna and Flo Rida, Nicki Minaj as featured artists respectively, so the certifications issued for these songs are added to the total amount of certified units for all involved artists. However, the certifications issued for songs that have been recorded by four or more artists are not included as the artists involved would have played minor roles, examples of such songs are Kanye West's "[Monster](Monster_(Kanye_West_song) "Monster (Kanye West song)")" and/or "[All Day](All_Day_(Kanye_West_song) "All Day (Kanye West song)")".[[lower-alpha 1]](List_of_best-selling_music_artists#cite_note-songs-9)

***Music to Be Murdered By*** is the eleventh [studio album](Studio_album "Studio album") by American rapper <Eminem>. It was released on January 17, 2020, through [Shady Records](Shady_Records "Shady Records"), [Aftermath Entertainment](Aftermath_Entertainment "Aftermath Entertainment"), and [Interscope Records](Interscope_Records "Interscope Records"). Just like Eminem's previous studio album *[Kamikaze](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album) "Kamikaze (Eminem album)")* (2018), the album was released with [no prior announcement](Surprise_album "Surprise album"). The album was produced by many producers, with Eminem and [Dr. Dre](Dr._Dre "Dr. Dre") serving as [executive producers](Executive_producer "Executive producer"). It features guest appearances from [Skylar Grey](Skylar_Grey "Skylar Grey"), [Young M.A](Young_M.A "Young M.A"), [Royce da 5'9"](Royce_da_5'9%22 "Royce da 5'9""), [White Gold](White_Gold_(musician) "White Gold (musician)"), [Ed Sheeran](Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran"), the late [Juice WRLD](Juice_Wrld "Juice Wrld"), [Black Thought](Black_Thought "Black Thought"), [Q-Tip](Q-Tip_(musician) "Q-Tip (musician)"), [Denaun](Mr._Porter "Mr. Porter"), [Anderson .Paak](Anderson_Paak "Anderson Paak"), [Don Toliver](Don_Toliver "Don Toliver"), [Kxng Crooked](Kxng_Crooked "Kxng Crooked") and [Joell Ortiz](Joell_Ortiz "Joell Ortiz"). The album's title, cover art, and concept are inspired by [Alfred Hitchcock](Alfred_Hitchcock "Alfred Hitchcock") and [Jeff Alexander](Jeff_Alexander "Jeff Alexander")'s 1958 spoken word album *Alfred Hitchcock Presents Music to Be Murdered By*. The album was supported by three singles: "[Darkness](Darkness_(Eminem_song) "Darkness (Eminem song)")", "[Godzilla](Godzilla_(Eminem_song) "Godzilla (Eminem song)")" and "[Those Kinda Nights](Those_Kinda_Nights "Those Kinda Nights")". Alongside the album's surprise release, Eminem also released the music video for "Darkness", which revolves around the [2017 Las Vegas shooting](2017_Las_Vegas_shooting "2017 Las Vegas shooting") from the point of view of the perpetrator [Stephen Paddock](Stephen_Paddock "Stephen Paddock") alternating with Eminem's own.

The album debuted at number one on the [*Billboard* 200](Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), selling 279,000 [album-equivalent units](Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit") in its first week. Subsequently, Eminem became the first artist to have ten consecutive number-one albums in the US and one of six artists to have released at least ten US number-one albums.[[7]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-BB200-7) *Music to Be Murdered By* reached number one in 16 countries. Music critics praised Eminem's lyrical abilities and the improved production after *Kamikaze*, while criticism was directed towards the album's formulaic song structure, lack of innovation, and shock value.

On December 18, 2020, Eminem released a deluxe version of the album, named *Music to Be Murdered By – Side B*, without any prior announcement. It includes the original album's 20 tracks along with 16 new ones. It includes a variety of features, with guest appearances from [Skylar Grey](Skylar_Grey "Skylar Grey"), [DJ Premier](DJ_Premier "DJ Premier"), [Ty Dolla $ign](Ty_Dolla_%24ign "Ty Dolla $ign"), [Dr. Dre](Dr._Dre "Dr. Dre"), Sly Pyper, MAJ, and [White Gold](White_Gold_(musician) "White Gold (musician)").

## Recording and production

In 2019, A&R representative [Mike "Heron" Herard](Mike_Herard "Mike Herard") of [Shady Records](Shady_Records "Shady Records") pursued production contributions for a new album by Eminem. This was a departure from his usual process at his company BeatleHustle, which manages [sample](Sampling_(music) "Sampling (music)") composers who send their beats to high-profile producers. Eventually, a group of producers had been enlisted for the project, including Eminem's longtime creative partners [Royce da 5'9"](Royce_da_5'9%22 "Royce da 5'9"") and [Dr. Dre](Dr._Dre "Dr. Dre"), as well as the latter's colleagues – Dawaun Parker, Lawrence Jr., Dem Jointz, Mista Choc, DJ Silk, and Erik Griggs – and young, burgeoning producers – D.A. Doman (producer of <Tyga>'s "[Taste](Taste_(Tyga_song) "Taste (Tyga song)")") and [Ricky Racks](Ricky_Racks "Ricky Racks") (producer of [Future](Future_(rapper) "Future (rapper)")'s "[Crushed Up](Crushed_Up "Crushed Up")").[[8]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-Leight-8)

According to a January 2020 *[Rolling Stone](Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* feature on the album's making, "Lawrence Jr. has been working sporadically with Dr. Dre since the rapper-producer left [Death Row Records](Death_Row_Records "Death Row Records") in the Nineties; starting in the summer, the drummer went into the studio with the rest of Dr. Dre's team to create a suite of tracks that ended up on the back half of *Music to Be Murdered By*." Lawrence Jr. told the magazine, "Dem Jointz is a producer, Eric Griggs plays keys, bass, and guitar, Dawaun Parker is a keyboard player and producer, myself, I'm a drummer. We know Dre's instincts, and he's the coach, the orchestrator."[[8]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-Leight-8)

Other collaborators for the album included [Black Thought](Black_Thought "Black Thought"), [Q-Tip](Q-Tip_(musician) "Q-Tip (musician)"), [Juice Wrld](Juice_Wrld "Juice Wrld"), [Ed Sheeran](Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran"), [Young M.A](Young_M.A "Young M.A"), [Skylar Grey](Skylar_Grey "Skylar Grey"), [Don Toliver](Don_Toliver "Don Toliver"), [Anderson .Paak](Anderson_.Paak "Anderson .Paak"), [Kxng Crooked](Kxng_Crooked "Kxng Crooked") and [Joell Ortiz](Joell_Ortiz "Joell Ortiz").[[9]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-9) On the track "[Godzilla](Godzilla_(Eminem_song) "Godzilla (Eminem song)")", Eminem recorded a third verse that broke the record for the fastest verse on a [charted](Record_charts "Record charts") track, rapping 10.65 syllables per second. [[10]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-GodzillaRecord-10) Eminem surpassed his own records held by his featured verse on [Nicki Minaj](Nicki_Minaj "Nicki Minaj")'s 2018 song "[Majesty](Majesty_(Nicki_Minaj_and_Labrinth_song) "Majesty (Nicki Minaj and Labrinth song)")", where he rapped 10.3 syllables per second, and his 2013 single "[Rap God](Rap_God "Rap God")", where he rapped 9.6 syllables per second.[[10]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-GodzillaRecord-10)

***Kamikaze*** (stylized as ***KAMIKAZƎ***) is the tenth [studio album](Studio_album "Studio album") by American rapper <Eminem>, released on August 31, 2018, through [Shady Records](Shady_Records "Shady Records"), [Aftermath Entertainment](Aftermath_Entertainment "Aftermath Entertainment"), and [Interscope Records](Interscope_Records "Interscope Records"). The album was released with [no prior announcement](Surprise_album "Surprise album"). It features guest appearances from [Joyner Lucas](Joyner_Lucas "Joyner Lucas"), [Royce da 5'9"](Royce_da_5'9%22 "Royce da 5'9""), [Jessie Reyez](Jessie_Reyez "Jessie Reyez"), and uncredited vocals by [Justin Vernon](Justin_Vernon "Justin Vernon") from the band [Bon Iver](Bon_Iver "Bon Iver"). Eminem, credited as Slim Shady, and [Dr. Dre](Dr._Dre "Dr. Dre") served as executive producers, while production was handled by Eminem himself alongside a variety of producers such as <Boi-1da>, [Tay Keith](Tay_Keith "Tay Keith"), [Ronny J](Ronny_J "Ronny J"), [Mike Will Made It](Mike_Will_Made_It "Mike Will Made It"), frequent collaborator [Luis Resto](Luis_Resto_(musician) "Luis Resto (musician)"), and others.[[3]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-3)

Following the polarizing reception of his previous album, *[Revival](Revival_(Eminem_album) "Revival (Eminem album)")* (2017), music journalists debated over whether the rapper's relevance and ability were waning. In response to the criticism, Eminem released a remix of the song "[Chloraseptic](Chloraseptic_(song) "Chloraseptic (song)")" in January 2018 featuring [2 Chainz](2_Chainz "2 Chainz") and <Phresher>. *Kamikaze* represents a continuation of this response, containing various insults against critics and rappers alike. The artwork is an homage to [Beastie Boys](Beastie_Boys "Beastie Boys")' debut album, *[Licensed to Ill](Licensed_to_Ill "Licensed to Ill")* (1986).

*Kamikaze* received mixed reviews from critics. Some praised it as an improvement over Eminem's previous album and a welcome return to his more aggressive style, while others criticized him for focusing too much on the reception of *Revival* throughout the album, and for his lack of adaption to the current sound of hip hop. The album also generated some controversy for its [diss tracks](Diss_track "Diss track") against various artists.

The album was promoted with three singles: "[Fall](Fall_(Eminem_song) "Fall (Eminem song)")", "[Venom](Venom_(Eminem_song) "Venom (Eminem song)")", from the [2018 movie of the same name](Venom_(2018_film) "Venom (2018 film)"), and "[Lucky You](Lucky_You_(song) "Lucky You (song)")", and a music video for ["Good Guy"](Good_Guy_(Eminem_song) "Good Guy (Eminem song)"), along with a supporting tour. Commercially, the album reached number one in 18 countries, becoming Eminem's ninth[[4]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-bb200-4) consecutive number-one album in the United States, and later becoming the best-selling hip-hop album of 2018. It later received [platinum](RIAA_certification "RIAA certification") certification by the [Recording Industry Association of America](Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") (RIAA).

## Recording and release

On January 8, 2018, Eminem unexpectedly released a remix to his *[Revival](Revival_(Eminem_album) "Revival (Eminem album)")* song "Chloraseptic", featuring [2 Chainz](2_Chainz "2 Chainz") and <Phresher>. In the song, Eminem mocked critics of *Revival*, concluding "I just added to the fuel in my rocket pack, till I'm ready to respond then I'ma launch it at 'em... I'll be back..." On January 22, 2018, photos revealed [Mike Will Made-It](Mike_Will_Made-It "Mike Will Made-It") in the studio with Eminem and Dr. Dre.[[5]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-bb-5) During the *Revival* sessions, [S1](Symbolyc_One "Symbolyc One") tried to work with Eminem but he refused; the producer kept sending him [beats](Musical_beat "Musical beat") to use on future tracks that the rapper incorporated into *Kamikaze* songs.[[6]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-s1-6) The afternoon before *Kamikaze*'s release, Eminem posted a 15-second teaser of a new song on social media, featuring the logo for the superhero film *[Venom](Venom_(2018_film) "Venom (2018 film)")*,[[7]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-venom-7) without comment.

On August 31, 2018, he released the album to digital music stores and streaming services without any promotion or pre-announcement, unlike the extensive marketing done for *Revival*;[[8]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-cst-8) he would repeat the strategy with 2020's *[Music to Be Murdered By](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By "Music to Be Murdered By")*. *[Billboard](Billboard_(magazine) "Billboard (magazine)")* credits the success of the [surprise release](Surprise_album "Surprise album") to Beyoncé's [self-titled fifth studio album](Beyonc%C3%A9_(album) "Beyoncé (album)") released in December 2013 without any promotion or pre-announcement, which was a critical and commercial success, ultimately changing the global release day for music from Tuesday to Friday.[[9]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-bbrelease-9) The album was sold on his website in several formats, including bundled with merchandise such as apparel.[[10]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-e!-10) Eminem used social media services such as <Instagram> and <Twitter> to announce the release[[11]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-release-11) and has relied on the extensive feedback from diss tracks and Internet hype to spread the word of the album.[[12]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-genius-12) Several weeks after the album's release and subsequent commercial success, Eminem took out a full-page ad in *[The Hollywood Reporter](The_Hollywood_Reporter "The Hollywood Reporter")* mocking negative reviews of *Kamikaze*, including *The Hollywood Reporter*'s review itself.[[13]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-ad-13)

Although he had no marketing prior to the debut,[[14]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-bbmarketing-14) Eminem had previously debuted [freestyle rap](Freestyle_rap "Freestyle rap") "The Storm"[[15]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-cbs-15) at the [2017 BET Hip Hop Awards](2017_BET_Hip_Hop_Awards "2017 BET Hip Hop Awards") using similar lyrics to the eventual title track[[16]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-kamikaze-16) and he directly referred to his experience performing it on "The Ringer".[[17]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-nyt-17) He debuted a clothing line featuring "The Kamikaze" t-shirt the month prior.[[18]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-xxlshirt-18) Producer Illa da Producer sees the album as similar to *[The Slim Shady LP](The_Slim_Shady_LP "The Slim Shady LP")* in terms of its ferocity, rather than the subdued *Revival*.[[19]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-illrs-19)

American singer [Justin Vernon](Justin_Vernon "Justin Vernon") of [Bon Iver](Bon_Iver "Bon Iver"), whose vocals were uncredited on the song "Fall", disavowed his participation in the album, claiming that he was not in the studio when the recording was made.[[20]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-jv-20) A [music video](Music_video "Music video") for "Fall" was released on September 4, 2018, addressing criticism of *Revival*.[[21]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-fall-21) The music video was directed by James Larese,[[21]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-fall-21) who previously directed the music videos of "[Framed](Framed_(Eminem_song) "Framed (Eminem song)")" and "[Caterpillar](Caterpillar_(song) "Caterpillar (song)")". A second video was released for "Lucky You" on September 13, 2018[[22]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-lyvid-22) followed by one for "[Venom](Venom_(Eminem_song) "Venom (Eminem song)")" on October 5, 2018[[23]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-venomvid-23) as well as one for "Good Guy" on December 7, 2018.[[24]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-ggvid-24)

***Revival*** is the ninth [studio album](Studio_album "Studio album") by American rapper <Eminem>. The album was released on December 15, 2017, through [Aftermath Entertainment](Aftermath_Entertainment "Aftermath Entertainment"), [Shady Records](Shady_Records "Shady Records") and [Interscope Records](Interscope_Records "Interscope Records").[[5]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-5) Production for the album took place during 2016 to 2017 at various recording studios. In addition to Eminem himself, music production was handled by various record producers, including [Rick Rubin](Rick_Rubin "Rick Rubin"), <Fredwreck>, [Skylar Grey](Skylar_Grey "Skylar Grey"), [Alex da Kid](Alex_da_Kid "Alex da Kid"), and executive producer [Dr. Dre](Dr._Dre "Dr. Dre").[[6]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-6) *Revival* features [guest appearances](Guest_appearance "Guest appearance") from artists [Beyoncé](Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé"), <Phresher>, [Ed Sheeran](Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran"), [Alicia Keys](Alicia_Keys "Alicia Keys"), [X Ambassadors](X_Ambassadors "X Ambassadors"), [Skylar Grey](Skylar_Grey "Skylar Grey"), <Kehlani>, and [Pink](Pink_(singer) "Pink (singer)").

Eminem first revealed that he was working on an album following the release of "[Campaign Speech](Campaign_Speech "Campaign Speech")" in October 2016. A year later, he performed a [viral](Viral_video "Viral video") freestyle at the [2017 BET Hip Hop Awards](2017_BET_Hip_Hop_Awards "2017 BET Hip Hop Awards"), criticizing then-President [Donald Trump](Donald_Trump "Donald Trump"). The album has many lines critiquing [Trump's presidential campaign](Donald_Trump_2016_presidential_campaign "Donald Trump 2016 presidential campaign") and [election](2016_United_States_presidential_election "2016 United States presidential election").

The album's lead single, "[Walk on Water](Walk_on_Water_(Eminem_song) "Walk on Water (Eminem song)")", featuring Beyoncé, was released on November 10, 2017. "[Untouchable](Untouchable_(Eminem_song) "Untouchable (Eminem song)")" was released as a promotional single a week prior to the album's release. *Revival* was leaked online on December 13, 2017, two days before the album's release date.[[7]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-7) The album issued several more singles, including "[River](River_(Eminem_song) "River (Eminem song)")", featuring Ed Sheeran, "[Nowhere Fast](Nowhere_Fast_(Eminem_song) "Nowhere Fast (Eminem song)")", featuring Kehlani, and "Remind Me".[[4]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-Radiodate-4) A music video for "[Framed](Framed_(Eminem_song) "Framed (Eminem song)")" was also released on April 3, 2018.

Reception to *Revival* was mixed to negative, with critics panning its [rock](Rock_music "Rock music")-influenced production on several songs and the heavy use of [pop](Pop_music "Pop music") artists for guest appearances. The album debuted at number one in Australia, Canada, Finland, the UK, and the US. In addition, it was the [UK Christmas number one album of 2017](List_of_UK_Albums_Chart_Christmas_number_ones "List of UK Albums Chart Christmas number ones") and has been certified [platinum](BPI_certification "BPI certification") in the UK.[[8]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-OCC-8) It was followed by *[Kamikaze](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album) "Kamikaze (Eminem album)")* (2018), Eminem's tenth studio album, in which he reacts to criticism of *Revival*.

## Background

Eminem first revealed that he was working on an album when he announced the song "[Campaign Speech](Campaign_Speech "Campaign Speech")" on his <Twitter> in October 2016, writing, "Don't worry I'm working on an album! Here's something meanwhile."[[9]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-9) Rumors about the release date started in late 2016, saying the album would be called *Success* and would be released sometime in January 2017.[[10]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-Capital_Xtra-10) A fake tracklist also was leaked at the same time, with <Adele>, [Chance the Rapper](Chance_the_Rapper "Chance the Rapper"), [Kid Cudi](Kid_Cudi "Kid Cudi"), [Vince Staples](Vince_Staples "Vince Staples"), [The Weeknd](The_Weeknd "The Weeknd") and Mástein Bennett as featured artists.[[11]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-11) Rumors were sparked again in February and March 2017, when Eminem announced he was headlining three shows in [Reading](Reading%2C_Berkshire "Reading, Berkshire"), <Glasgow> and <Leeds>.[[12]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-12)[[13]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-13) Various news articles said that because he was performing, he would have to release new material to perform, or at least preview, at the festivals.[[14]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-14)

***Music to Be Murdered By*** is the eleventh [studio album](Studio_album "Studio album") by American rapper <Eminem>. It was released on January 17, 2020, through [Shady Records](Shady_Records "Shady Records"), [Aftermath Entertainment](Aftermath_Entertainment "Aftermath Entertainment"), and [Interscope Records](Interscope_Records "Interscope Records"). Just like Eminem's previous studio album *[Kamikaze](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album) "Kamikaze (Eminem album)")* (2018), the album was released with [no prior announcement](Surprise_album "Surprise album"). The album was produced by many producers, with Eminem and [Dr. Dre](Dr._Dre "Dr. Dre") serving as [executive producers](Executive_producer "Executive producer"). It features guest appearances from [Skylar Grey](Skylar_Grey "Skylar Grey"), [Young M.A](Young_M.A "Young M.A"), [Royce da 5'9"](Royce_da_5'9%22 "Royce da 5'9""), [White Gold](White_Gold_(musician) "White Gold (musician)"), [Ed Sheeran](Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran"), the late [Juice WRLD](Juice_Wrld "Juice Wrld"), [Black Thought](Black_Thought "Black Thought"), [Q-Tip](Q-Tip_(musician) "Q-Tip (musician)"), [Denaun](Mr._Porter "Mr. Porter"), [Anderson .Paak](Anderson_Paak "Anderson Paak"), [Don Toliver](Don_Toliver "Don Toliver"), [Kxng Crooked](Kxng_Crooked "Kxng Crooked") and [Joell Ortiz](Joell_Ortiz "Joell Ortiz"). The album's title, cover art, and concept are inspired by [Alfred Hitchcock](Alfred_Hitchcock "Alfred Hitchcock") and [Jeff Alexander](Jeff_Alexander "Jeff Alexander")'s 1958 spoken word album *Alfred Hitchcock Presents Music to Be Murdered By*. The album was supported by three singles: "[Darkness](Darkness_(Eminem_song) "Darkness (Eminem song)")", "[Godzilla](Godzilla_(Eminem_song) "Godzilla (Eminem song)")" and "[Those Kinda Nights](Those_Kinda_Nights "Those Kinda Nights")". Alongside the album's surprise release, Eminem also released the music video for "Darkness", which revolves around the [2017 Las Vegas shooting](2017_Las_Vegas_shooting "2017 Las Vegas shooting") from the point of view of the perpetrator [Stephen Paddock](Stephen_Paddock "Stephen Paddock") alternating with Eminem's own.

The album debuted at number one on the [*Billboard* 200](Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), selling 279,000 [album-equivalent units](Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit") in its first week. Subsequently, Eminem became the first artist to have ten consecutive number-one albums in the US and one of six artists to have released at least ten US number-one albums.[[7]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-BB200-7) *Music to Be Murdered By* reached number one in 16 countries. Music critics praised Eminem's lyrical abilities and the improved production after *Kamikaze*, while criticism was directed towards the album's formulaic song structure, lack of innovation, and shock value.

On December 18, 2020, Eminem released a deluxe version of the album, named *Music to Be Murdered By – Side B*, without any prior announcement. It includes the original album's 20 tracks along with 16 new ones. It includes a variety of features, with guest appearances from [Skylar Grey](Skylar_Grey "Skylar Grey"), [DJ Premier](DJ_Premier "DJ Premier"), [Ty Dolla $ign](Ty_Dolla_%24ign "Ty Dolla $ign"), [Dr. Dre](Dr._Dre "Dr. Dre"), Sly Pyper, MAJ, and [White Gold](White_Gold_(musician) "White Gold (musician)").

## Recording and production

In 2019, A&R representative [Mike "Heron" Herard](Mike_Herard "Mike Herard") of [Shady Records](Shady_Records "Shady Records") pursued production contributions for a new album by Eminem. This was a departure from his usual process at his company BeatleHustle, which manages [sample](Sampling_(music) "Sampling (music)") composers who send their beats to high-profile producers. Eventually, a group of producers had been enlisted for the project, including Eminem's longtime creative partners [Royce da 5'9"](Royce_da_5'9%22 "Royce da 5'9"") and [Dr. Dre](Dr._Dre "Dr. Dre"), as well as the latter's colleagues – Dawaun Parker, Lawrence Jr., Dem Jointz, Mista Choc, DJ Silk, and Erik Griggs – and young, burgeoning producers – D.A. Doman (producer of <Tyga>'s "[Taste](Taste_(Tyga_song) "Taste (Tyga song)")") and [Ricky Racks](Ricky_Racks "Ricky Racks") (producer of [Future](Future_(rapper) "Future (rapper)")'s "[Crushed Up](Crushed_Up "Crushed Up")").[[8]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-Leight-8)

According to a January 2020 *[Rolling Stone](Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* feature on the album's making, "Lawrence Jr. has been working sporadically with Dr. Dre since the rapper-producer left [Death Row Records](Death_Row_Records "Death Row Records") in the Nineties; starting in the summer, the drummer went into the studio with the rest of Dr. Dre's team to create a suite of tracks that ended up on the back half of *Music to Be Murdered By*." Lawrence Jr. told the magazine, "Dem Jointz is a producer, Eric Griggs plays keys, bass, and guitar, Dawaun Parker is a keyboard player and producer, myself, I'm a drummer. We know Dre's instincts, and he's the coach, the orchestrator."[[8]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-Leight-8)

Other collaborators for the album included [Black Thought](Black_Thought "Black Thought"), [Q-Tip](Q-Tip_(musician) "Q-Tip (musician)"), [Juice Wrld](Juice_Wrld "Juice Wrld"), [Ed Sheeran](Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran"), [Young M.A](Young_M.A "Young M.A"), [Skylar Grey](Skylar_Grey "Skylar Grey"), [Don Toliver](Don_Toliver "Don Toliver"), [Anderson .Paak](Anderson_.Paak "Anderson .Paak"), [Kxng Crooked](Kxng_Crooked "Kxng Crooked") and [Joell Ortiz](Joell_Ortiz "Joell Ortiz").[[9]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-9) On the track "[Godzilla](Godzilla_(Eminem_song) "Godzilla (Eminem song)")", Eminem recorded a third verse that broke the record for the fastest verse on a [charted](Record_charts "Record charts") track, rapping 10.65 syllables per second. [[10]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-GodzillaRecord-10) Eminem surpassed his own records held by his featured verse on [Nicki Minaj](Nicki_Minaj "Nicki Minaj")'s 2018 song "[Majesty](Majesty_(Nicki_Minaj_and_Labrinth_song) "Majesty (Nicki Minaj and Labrinth song)")", where he rapped 10.3 syllables per second, and his 2013 single "[Rap God](Rap_God "Rap God")", where he rapped 9.6 syllables per second.[[10]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-GodzillaRecord-10)

## Title and cover

The album's title and alternative cover art share the same concept as the 1958 album *Alfred Hitchcock Presents Music to Be Murdered By*, which interspersed audio of the director [Alfred Hitchcock](Alfred_Hitchcock "Alfred Hitchcock")'s wry, dark humor into [easy listening](Easy_listening "Easy listening") instrumentals arranged by [Jeff Alexander](Jeff_Alexander "Jeff Alexander").[[11]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-Variety-11) Eminem tweeted an image of the 1958 album cover featuring Hitchcock holding an axe and a gun to his head and stated that his album's alternative cover was "inspired by the master, Uncle Alfred!"[[12]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-Complex-12) Audio of Hitchcock's voice from the 1958 album is sampled in the interludes "Alfred" and "Alfred (Outro)" and the beginning of the track "Little Engine".[[11]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-Variety-11) Both the 1958 and 2020 albums end with Hitchcock stating, "If you haven't been murdered, I can only say better luck next time. If you have been, goodnight, wherever you are."[[11]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-Variety-11) [Mark Beech](Mark_Beech_(writer) "Mark Beech (writer)") of *<Forbes>* magazine connected the alternate cover to this album's concept of murder and violence.[[13]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-13)

The album has three covers; the digital cover features Eminem posing with a shovel, wearing a [suit](Suit "Suit") and a [fedora](Fedora "Fedora"). The album's alternate cover features Eminem pointing a gun and holding an axe to his head.[[11]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-Variety-11) The physical CD cover features Eminem, hatless, posing with his hands behind his back. In the packaging, Eminem dedicates the album to rapper [Juice Wrld](Juice_Wrld "Juice Wrld"),[[14]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-Dedicate-14) who died from an accidental drug overdose on December 8, 2019,[[15]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-15) and Eminem's former bodyguard CeeAaqil Allah Barnes who also died.[[14]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-Dedicate-14) Juice Wrld's feature on "Godzilla" marked his first posthumous release.[[16]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-16)

## Release

The album was released on January 17, 2020, by [Shady Records](Shady_Records "Shady Records"), [Aftermath Entertainment](Aftermath_Entertainment "Aftermath Entertainment") and [Interscope Records](Interscope_Records "Interscope Records"). It was released as a surprise with no prior announcement, similarly to his previous and tenth studio album *[Kamikaze](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album) "Kamikaze (Eminem album)")* (2018).[[17]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-17) Alongside the album's release, Eminem also released a music video for "[Darkness](Darkness_(Eminem_song) "Darkness (Eminem song)")",[[18]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-18) directed by James Larese.[[12]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-Complex-12) The video, which revolves around the [2017 Las Vegas shooting](2017_Las_Vegas_shooting "2017 Las Vegas shooting") from the point of view of the perpetrator [Stephen Paddock](Stephen_Paddock "Stephen Paddock") alternating with Eminem's own, garnered appraisal but controversy too.[[19]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-:0-19) On January 31, 2020, "Godzilla" was released as a single,[[5]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-godzilla-5) with a music video directed by [Cole Bennett](Cole_Bennett "Cole Bennett") later being released on March 6.[[20]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-20)

On December 18, 2020, a deluxe Side B edition of the album, titled ***Music to Be Murdered By – Side B***, was released. Similar to Eminem's previous two albums, it was released without any prior announcement.[[48]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-sideb-48) It contains a bonus disc with sixteen new tracks, with guest appearances by [Skylar Grey](Skylar_Grey "Skylar Grey"), [DJ Premier](DJ_Premier "DJ Premier"), [Ty Dolla $ign](Ty_Dolla_Sign "Ty Dolla Sign"), [Dr. Dre](Dr._Dre "Dr. Dre"), Sly Pyper, MAJ, and White Gold.[[48]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-sideb-48)[[49]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-vulture-49) The album's release was accompanied by a music video for "[Gnat](Gnat_(song) "Gnat (song)")", directed by [Cole Bennett](Cole_Bennett "Cole Bennett").[[50]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-50) The music video for "[Higher](Higher_(Eminem_song) "Higher (Eminem song)")" premiered on January 23, 2021.[[51]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-51) Lyric videos for "Alfred's Theme" and "Tone Deaf" were also released, in the latter song Mathers pays tribute to the late Chicago rapper [King Von](King_Von "King Von").[[52]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-52)[[53]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-53)[[54]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-54). In May 2021, a remix of "[Killer](Killer_(Eminem_song) "Killer (Eminem song)")", featuring [Jack Harlow](Jack_Harlow "Jack Harlow") and <Cordae>, was released.[[55]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-55)

The week the deluxe edition was released, the album saw a 1,125% boost in sale units from the previous week, moving 94,000 units.[[56]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-56) This brought the album back up to the 3rd spot on the *Billboard 200* album chart in its 48th week, a 196 spot jump from the week previous, breaking a 50-year-old Billboard 200 record previously held by [Bob Dylan](Bob_Dylan "Bob Dylan") with *[Self Portrait](Self_Portrait_(Bob_Dylan_album) "Self Portrait (Bob Dylan album)")* (1970) which made a 193 spot jump.[[57]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-57)

*Side B* was met with generally positive reviews.[[58]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-MC-58) [Robert Christgau](Robert_Christgau "Robert Christgau") appraised the release as "more proof that Eminem loves rhyme as compulsively as [MF DOOM](MF_Doom "MF Doom") himself", adding that, "If he's not as playful or surreal about it as Doom, he sure does enunciate better, with a timbral dexterity never quashed by the rock-inflected production style that Dr. Dre laid on him decades ago and oversees here." While highlighting lyrics from "Alfred's Theme", "Tone Deaf", "Black Magic", and "These Demons" on *Side B*, he also observed "more braggadocio and less delight in these words for their own sake than in the Side A's".[[59]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-CG-59)

## Commercial performance

In the United States, *Kamikaze* opened at number one on the [*Billboard* 200](Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") with 434,000 [album-equivalent units](Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit"),[[56]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-bbnielsen-56) consisting of 252,000 traditional album sales as well as 225 million streams, giving Eminem his largest amount of streams within a week. This put him in the top ten for highest first week sales of 2018.[[57]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-stream-57) It became his ninth consecutive number-one album in the country, tying him with [Garth Brooks](Garth_Brooks "Garth Brooks") and [The Rolling Stones](The_Rolling_Stones "The Rolling Stones") for fifth-most entries to top the chart, and had the year's fifth-highest first-week sales in the USA.[[4]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-bb200-4) He also topped the [Artist 100](Artist_100 "Artist 100") chart due to album sales and song streams.[[58]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-artist100-58) The album dropped one place to number two in its second week behind [Paul McCartney](Paul_McCartney "Paul McCartney")'s *[Egypt Station](Egypt_Station "Egypt Station")*, earning an additional 136,000 album-equivalent units.[[59]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-bb2nd-59) All eleven songs entered the [*Billboard* Hot 100](Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"),[[60]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-allsongs-60) with "Lucky You" and "The Ringer" reaching numbers six and eight on the chart.[[61]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-hot100-61) He is the fifth artist to debut two songs in its top 10 simultaneously.[[62]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-fifth-62) By October 17, it was the best-selling hip hop album of the year[[63]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-rec-63) and a few days later, it was certified platinum by the [Recording Industry Association of America](Recording_Industry_Association_of_America "Recording Industry Association of America") with 1 million album-equivalent units in the United States; 415,000 of them being pure sales.[[64]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-plat-64)

The album also entered atop the [UK Albums Chart](UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart") on September 7, with first week sales of 55,000 album equivalent units, including 30,000 album-equivalent streams, making *Kamikaze* the United Kingdom's fifth-most streamed album in an opening week.[[65]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-surpass-65)[[66]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-ukofficial-66) As a result, Eminem surpassed [Led Zeppelin](Led_Zeppelin "Led Zeppelin") and <ABBA> for the most consecutive albums to reach the nation's summit,[[65]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-surpass-65) with nine.[[67]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-reuters-67) It was also the top album in Scotland.[[68]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartuk-sc-68) The following week, the album retained the top spot, with 51% of its consumption coming from streams[[69]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-uk2nd-69) and garnered 29,000 units for the third week to stay at number one.[[70]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-uk3rd-70) It managed to stay atop the charts for four weeks.[[71]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-uk4th-71) It was the 10th best-selling album of 2018 in the United Kingdom.[[72]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-uksales-72)

It additionally debuted at the top of the [ARIA Albums Chart](ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts"), giving Eminem his ninth number-one album in Australia[[73]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-ariadebut-73) (where it stayed for four weeks)[[74]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-australia4th-74) and the [Canadian Albums Chart](Canadian_Albums_Chart "Canadian Albums Chart"), becoming Eminem's 10th number-one album in Canada after debuting with 44,000 album-equivalent units.[[75]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-fyimusicnews-75) Other international charts that it topped include Austria,[[76]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartat-76) Belgium (<Flanders> only;[[77]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartbg-fl-77) it reached third in <Wallonia>[[78]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartbg-wa-78)), the Czech Republic,[[79]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartcz-79) Denmark, Finland,[[80]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartso-80) Ireland,[[81]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartie-81) Italy,[[82]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartit-82) the Netherlands,[[83]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartnl-83) New Zealand,[[84]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartnz-84) Norway,[[85]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartno-85) Sweden,[[86]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartse-86) and Switzerland;[[87]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartch-87) it retained top spot in Ireland the following[[88]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-ie2nd-88) two weeks.[[89]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-ie3rd-89) *Kamikaze* debuted at sixth in France, fourth in Germany,[[79]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartcz-79) tenth in Greece, eighth in Hungary, third in Poland, and fifteenth in Spain;[[90]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-chartes-90) after one week, it rose to second in Germany, and twelfth in Spain.

In 2018, *Kamikaze* was ranked as the 17th most popular album of the year on the *Billboard* 200[[94]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-bb2018-94) and by the end of the year *Kamikaze* had sold over 1,014,000 album-equivalent units in the US, with over 457,000 being pure sales.[[95]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-hdd-95) As of January 2019, *Kamikaze* has sold over 500,000 copies in pure sales, making it the only solo album of 2018 to do so.[[96]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-500k-96) According to the [International Federation of the Phonographic Industry](International_Federation_of_the_Phonographic_Industry "International Federation of the Phonographic Industry"), *Kamikaze* was the ninth best-selling album globally of 2018, with 1 million physical and digital copies sold.[[97]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-ifpi2018-97)

Throughout the album, lyrics criticize other musicians[[98]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-list-98)[[99]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-vibe-99) and several have responded publicly.[[100]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-bad-100) Eminem and rapper [Machine Gun Kelly](Machine_Gun_Kelly_(rapper) "Machine Gun Kelly (rapper)") have had an ongoing feud for several years,[[101]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-cosmo-101)[[102]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-feud-102) and Kelly released a [diss track](Diss_track "Diss track") in response to "Not Alike" titled "[Rap Devil](Rap_Devil "Rap Devil")" on September 3;[[103]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-diss-103) both songs were produced by [Ronny J](Ronny_J "Ronny J").[[104]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-prod-104) Kelly continued the feud at a concert, calling it "a battle between the past and the fucking future".[[105]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-mgk-105) The song's title refers to Eminem's "[Rap God](Rap_God "Rap God")" and Eminem went into the studio days later to record his own response,[[106]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-studio-106) as did former <D12> associate [Bizarre](Bizarre_(rapper) "Bizarre (rapper)").[[107]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-bizarre-107)[[108]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-bizdiss-108) Eminem responded with "[Killshot](Killshot_(Eminem_song) "Killshot (Eminem song)")" on September 14[[109]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-ks-109) and Bizarre's "Love Tap" was released on September 20.[[110]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-love-110) "Killshot" garnered 38.1 million streams on <YouTube> in its first 24 hours and over 80 million views in its first week, making it the most successful debut for a hip hop song (at the time) and the third-biggest debut in the platform's history. [Ja Rule](Ja_Rule "Ja Rule") responded on social media, re-igniting a feud the two had 15 years prior.[[113]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-jr-113) <6ix9ine>, [Iggy Azalea](Iggy_Azalea "Iggy Azalea"),[[114]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-ia-114) [Joe Budden](Joe_Budden "Joe Budden"),[[115]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-jb-115) [Die Antwoord](Die_Antwoord "Die Antwoord"),[[116]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-da-116) [Lupe Fiasco](Lupe_Fiasco "Lupe Fiasco"),[[117]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-lf-117) and [Lord Jamar](Lord_Jamar "Lord Jamar")[[118]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-lj-118) have also responded publicly, with the first releasing the skit "Legend" that raps over Eminem's "[Lose Yourself](Lose_Yourself "Lose Yourself")".[[119]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-6diss-119) Artists including [50 Cent](50_Cent "50 Cent")[[120]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-50cent-120) and [Remy Ma](Remy_Ma "Remy Ma")[[121]](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-remy-121) have come out in support of Eminem.

Upon release, *Revival* generally polarized music critics, as many were divided over its perceived lack of focus, lyrics, heavy sampling of rock music in the production, and the abundance of [pop](Pop_music "Pop music") artists for guest appearances.[[63]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-65) At <Metacritic>, which assigns a [normalized](Standard_score "Standard score") rating out of 100 to reviews from mainstream publications, the album received an [average](Weighted_arithmetic_mean "Weighted arithmetic mean") score of 50, based on 24 reviews, indicating "mixed or average" reviews.[[52]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-Metacritic-54)

Don Needham of *[The Guardian](The_Guardian "The Guardian")* criticized the album's production and focus, stating that "If Eminem thinks his verbal box of tricks can overcome the weakness of any backing track, his recent albums get demonstrated otherwise."[[57]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-TheGuardian-59) In a positive review, Andy Gill of *[The Independent](The_Independent "The Independent")* complimented the album's lyrical themes: "But ultimately, it's all about Eminem himself, and nowhere more dynamically than in the berserk self-assessment "Offended", where he asserts, amongst other things, that if the time he spent writing were taken into account, he'd be a minimum-wage slave – a faintly ludicrous claim, but immediately backed up by a bravura extended burst of rapid-rap babble that both explains and exemplifies his skills, and leaves one wondering not just how long it took to write, but how on earth he manages to pronounce such a polysyllabic torrent so perfectly."[[58]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-Independentreview-60) [Neil McCormick](Neil_McCormick "Neil McCormick") of *[The Daily Telegraph](The_Daily_Telegraph "The Daily Telegraph")* stated that *Revival* "represents Eminem on top form, which is to say unstoppable, unbeatable yet often indefensible."[[56]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-Telegraph-58)

*[The Irish Times](The_Irish_Times "The Irish Times")* concluded that *Revival* is "mildly more admirable than previous outings but no more enjoyable. A chance to bust out of the slump has passed Eminem by. It just might never happen for him."[[2]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-IrishTimes-2) In a mixed review, [Jon Caramanica](Jon_Caramanica "Jon Caramanica") of *[The New York Times](The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")* remarked that while the album is "probably the best of his recent albums", he criticized Eminem's apparent lack of awareness to the evolution of hip hop's sound in general, arguing that he is too "beholden to his own aesthetic."[[64]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-66) In a negative review, *[Consequence of Sound](Consequence_of_Sound "Consequence of Sound")* gave the album an "F" rating, calling the album "ugly, arthritic, and pleasureless" and "a disaster".[[55]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-CoS-57)

Comparing *Revival* to Eminem's previous bodies of work, Matthew Ismael Ruiz of *[Pitchfork](Pitchfork_Media "Pitchfork Media")* stated that "Musically, *Revival* is no different, chock full of piano ballads and pop-star features that echo the most cynically commercial corners of his catalog. The shock value comes not from the album's overwhelmingly bland hooks or cringe-worthy humor (of which there is plenty), but from the moments where his growth as a human is most apparent", concluding that "*Revival* is another late-career album that does little for his legacy."[[61]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-Pitchfork-63) Writing for *[Vice](Vice_(magazine) "Vice (magazine)")*, [Robert Christgau](Robert_Christgau "Robert Christgau") found the album "much cleverer than lemmings claim, bluntly and intelligently political too, but so received in its cartoon misogyny and pop grandeur you know he felt irrelevance bearing down even before [#MeToo](Me_Too_movement "Me Too movement") killed this album on the vine". He singled out "Untouchable", "Chloraseptic", and "Like Home" as highlights.[[65]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-67)

Trent Clark from *<HipHopDX>* said that "Eminem's dedication to wrecking mics like [Robert Mueller](Robert_Mueller "Robert Mueller") can never be questioned but the production choices still remain an enigma. When he doesn't bath in lamely visible rock samples like Joan Jett and the Blackhearts' "I Love Rock 'n' Roll" or The Cranberries' "Zombie" (on "Remind Me" or "In Your Head" respectively), he's mostly square pegging his intensified lyrics on mechanical slabs of assembly line pop hybrids." He singled out "Framed" and "Castle" as highlights:
> it's largely the retreads of past glory where he hits his stride the hardest. On the hypnotically-produced "Framed," Marshall dons the hockey mask for old times sake and pulls up off homicidal fantasies that for better or worse, feature the album's most in-pocket rhyme moment. And when he plunges into his drug-altered psyche to speak on his greatest love — his daughter Haile Jade — the ever-reliable [DJ Khalil](DJ_Khalil "DJ Khalil") steps up to the plate on "Castle" with a darkened soundbed of macabre guitars and deathly drum marches that feature the album's most vintage Eminem moment.[[66]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-68)

Mitch Findlay from *<HotNewHipHop>* wrote: "*Revival* is, by far, Eminem's most pop-friendly album to date. While previous albums merely flirted with the sound, *Revival* has bought a ring and proposed to it. Therefore, if you're somebody who finds no pleasure in the production of 'pop-rap,' you'll find no solace here." He singled out "Framed," "Castle" and "Arose" as highlights, with the latter two being "among *Revival*'s strongest tracks. Conceptually and lyrically, the closing pair find Eminem in excellent form, and longtime fans will no doubt cite these two as album highlights."[[67]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-69)

## Commercial performance

*Revival* is Eminem's eighth consecutive album to top the US [*Billboard* 200](Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), debuting with 267,000 album-equivalent units, 197,000 being traditional album sales. As a result, Eminem became the first musical act to get eight entries in a row debut at its summit.[[68]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-US_debut-70)

*Revival* entered atop the [UK Albums Chart](UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart") with 132,000 [album-equivalent units](Album-equivalent_units "Album-equivalent units"), becoming the year's second largest opening behind Ed Sheeran's *[÷](%C3%B7_(album) "÷ (album)")* and giving the rapper his eighth consecutive number-one album.[[8]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-OCC-8) As of October 2018, it sold 321,000 album-equivalent units in the UK.[[69]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-UK_Sales-71)

It additionally arrived at number one in Australia, becoming his ninth entry to top the [ARIA Albums Chart](ARIA_Charts "ARIA Charts").[[70]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-72) The album then fell behind *÷* the following week.[[71]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-73)

In 2018, *Revival* was ranked as the 32nd most popular album of the year on the *Billboard* 200.[[72]](Revival_(Eminem_album)#cite_note-74)

# Multi-Agent Delegation

When the user asks a complex question, do not attempt to answer it yourself. Break it up into smaller pieces, then use the `fork` tool to delegate each piece to a subagent. You MUST use the `join` tool to retrieve the subagent's result for each subagent you create with `fork`. Each subagent has access to the exact same tools that you do.

If you are confident you can answer the user's query without help, do not use the delegation tools.

The instructions you give to each subagent SHOULD be a smaller piece of the instructions you were given. Do not delegate your full task to a subagent. Subagents do not have access to the information you have retrieved in prior turns or your thoughts. You must provide each subagent with the necessary context it needs in its instructions.

Your instructions to a subagent can be long, up to about 5000 characters. Each subagent is as capable as you are, but starts with a blank slate, so you must provide it specific and detailed information in its instructions.

- Implement the `dfs()` function.
- Use the article to list the subway connections.

- Continue searching for the magic number.

***Music to Be Murdered By*** is the eleventh [studio album](Studio_album "Studio album") by American rapper <Eminem>. It was released on January 17, 2020, through [Shady Records](Shady_Records "Shady Records"), [Aftermath Entertainment](Aftermath_Entertainment "Aftermath Entertainment"), and [Interscope Records](Interscope_Records "Interscope Records"). Just like Eminem's previous studio album *[Kamikaze](Kamikaze_(Eminem_album) "Kamikaze (Eminem album)")* (2018), the album was released with [no prior announcement](Surprise_album "Surprise album"). The album was produced by many producers, with Eminem and [Dr. Dre](Dr._Dre "Dr. Dre") serving as [executive producers](Executive_producer "Executive producer"). It features guest appearances from [Skylar Grey](Skylar_Grey "Skylar Grey"), [Young M.A](Young_M.A "Young M.A"), [Royce da 5'9"](Royce_da_5'9%22 "Royce da 5'9""), [White Gold](White_Gold_(musician) "White Gold (musician)"), [Ed Sheeran](Ed_Sheeran "Ed Sheeran"), the late [Juice WRLD](Juice_Wrld "Juice Wrld"), [Black Thought](Black_Thought "Black Thought"), [Q-Tip](Q-Tip_(musician) "Q-Tip (musician)"), [Denaun](Mr._Porter "Mr. Porter"), [Anderson .Paak](Anderson_Paak "Anderson Paak"), [Don Toliver](Don_Toliver "Don Toliver"), [Kxng Crooked](Kxng_Crooked "Kxng Crooked") and [Joell Ortiz](Joell_Ortiz "Joell Ortiz"). The album's title, cover art, and concept are inspired by [Alfred Hitchcock](Alfred_Hitchcock "Alfred Hitchcock") and [Jeff Alexander](Jeff_Alexander "Jeff Alexander")'s 1958 spoken word album *Alfred Hitchcock Presents Music to Be Murdered By*. The album was supported by three singles: "[Darkness](Darkness_(Eminem_song) "Darkness (Eminem song)")", "[Godzilla](Godzilla_(Eminem_song) "Godzilla (Eminem song)")" and "[Those Kinda Nights](Those_Kinda_Nights "Those Kinda Nights")". Alongside the album's surprise release, Eminem also released the music video for "Darkness", which revolves around the [2017 Las Vegas shooting](2017_Las_Vegas_shooting "2017 Las Vegas shooting") from the point of view of the perpetrator [Stephen Paddock](Stephen_Paddock "Stephen Paddock") alternating with Eminem's own.

The album debuted at number one on the [*Billboard* 200](Billboard_200 "Billboard 200"), selling 279,000 [album-equivalent units](Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit") in its first week. he star-studded, commercially sustainable album *[Recovery](Recovery_(Eminem_album) "Recovery (Eminem album)")* was, but that isn't necessarily a bad thing. On this album, despite its handful of flaws, Em shows strong signs of adapting to the times through modern musical choices and smarter songwriting."[[34]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-hiphopdx-34) *[Consequence of Sound](Consequence_of_Sound "Consequence of Sound")*'s Dan Weiss was generally positive, and, about the album's themes, he said that "If he's figuring out from scratch how to be a compelling artist again, Eminem's improved the caliber of his beats and guests, taking stands against the right day-to-day injustices, toning down the tasteless (with the exception of the already-infamous Ariana line, of course), and rapping with the manic precision of someone who just snorted a whole sandcastle of cocaine and [Vyvanse](Lisdexamfetamine "Lisdexamfetamine"). If only a single minute of it was as hilarious or bracing as Chris D'Elia's impression of him."[[35]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-COS-35) Similarly, Fred Thomas of <AllMusic> opined, "*Music to Be Murdered By* sees Eminem pulling himself out of *Kamikaze*'s wreckage somewhat, though he still falls victim to moments of willful dumbness and a tedious self-obsession that's become par for the course. On the album's best tracks, there are still hints of the fire that made Eminem a rap legend."[[23]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-AllMusic-23)

*[Entertainment Weekly](Entertainment_Weekly "Entertainment Weekly")*'s Christopher R. Weingarten was more critical, stating that, "As a whole, *Music to Be Murdered By* is as hit-and-miss as anything Eminem has released this side of the millennium. But remove the skits, the relationship songs, the family songs, the morose gun control song, and the quirky Ed Sheeran club goof and you still have 36 solid minutes of the daffy, one-of-a-kind rap genius that keeps captivating true-school heads and longtime fans. Or, if you'd like, keep it all and you still have the most solid work he's done in a few years."[[27]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-EW-27) *<NME>*'s Jordan Basset was ambivalent towards the album's lyrical themes and stated, "He splits the difference on *Music To Be Murdered By*, indulging his immature ego (griping at bad reviews, stirring controversy for the sake of it) even as he offers salient social criticism and admits his missteps. He's ready to pass on hard-earned wisdom before running his mouth like he hasn't learned his own lessons. And he offers casual fans a hook or two before embarking on another lyrical work-out."[[30]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-NME-30) Paul A. Thompson of *[Pitchfork](Pitchfork_(website) "Pitchfork (website)")* said that the album "is not, strictly speaking, a good record—Eminem hasn't made one of those in a decade—but his latest boasts enough technical command and generates just enough arresting ideas to hold your attention."[[31]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-pitchfork-31)

### Controversy

The song "[Darkness](Darkness_(Eminem_song) "Darkness (Eminem song)")", about the [2017 Las Vegas shooting](2017_Las_Vegas_shooting "2017 Las Vegas shooting") and told from the point of view of the shooter [Stephen Paddock](Stephen_Paddock "Stephen Paddock") alternating with Eminem's own, has garnered particular attention and critical acclaim.[[19]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-:0-19)

The lyrics of "Unaccommodating", in which Eminem referenced the 2017 [Manchester Arena bombing](Manchester_Arena_bombing "Manchester Arena bombing"), drew significant criticism, with many critics finding the lyrics objectionable. The [Mayor of Greater Manchester](Mayor_of_Greater_Manchester "Mayor of Greater Manchester") [Andy Burnham](Andy_Burnham "Andy Burnham") denounced the song's lyrics, describing them as "unnecessarily hurtful and deeply disrespectful." The lyrics also drew widespread criticism from victims' relatives and others involved in the attack.[[36]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-36)

Roisin O'Connor of *[The Independent](The_Independent "The Independent")* gave the album a negative review, and criticized the album by saying, "Eminem belittles the trauma of a then 26-year-old [Ariana Grande](Ariana_Grande "Ariana Grande") for kicks on 'Unaccommodating' by comparing himself to the [Manchester Arena bomber](Manchester_Arena_bombing#Attacker "Manchester Arena bombing"). The sour taste of this track lingers well beyond the album's centrepiece, 'Darkness', which is intended as a searing critique of [America's toxic gun culture](Gun_culture_in_the_United_States "Gun culture in the United States"). Instead, his use of gunfire and explosion samples feels grossly exploitative."[[29]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-Independent-29)[[37]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-37)

## Commercial performance

In the United States, *Music to Be Murdered By* debuted at number one on the US [*Billboard* 200](Billboard_200 "Billboard 200") chart, earning 279,000 [album-equivalent units](Album-equivalent_unit "Album-equivalent unit") (including 117,000 copies as traditional album sales) in its first week.[[7]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-BB200-7) This became Eminem's tenth US number-one album and made him one of six artists to have released at least ten number-one albums.[[7]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-BB200-7) The album also accumulated a total of 217.6 million on-demand streams for the album's tracks.[[7]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-BB200-7) As of December 2020, *Music to Be Murdered By* had sold over 1,053,000 equivalent units, including 249,000 in pure sales.[[38]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-38)[[39]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-39)

Eventually, *Music to Be Murdered By* was the 9th best-selling album (in pure sales) of 2020 in the United States, with 287,000 copies.[[40]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-40)

The album debuted at number-one in other countries. It became Eminem's 11th number-one album in Canada, while debuting atop the [Canadian Albums Chart](Canadian_Albums_Chart "Canadian Albums Chart") with 33,000 album-equivalent units.[[41]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-41) The album remained at the top spot in Canada for four straight weeks, the longest for an Eminem album since *Recovery*.[[42]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-42)[[43]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-43) It also entered at number one on the [UK Albums Chart](UK_Albums_Chart "UK Albums Chart") with first week sales of 36,000 album equivalent units, making Eminem the first artist to release 10 consecutive number one albums in the UK. He also achieved a chart double with *Godzilla* debuting at number one on the [UK Singles Chart](UK_Singles_Chart "UK Singles Chart").[[44]](Music_to_Be_Murdered_By#cite_note-44)
